Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
вода
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *wed-
Proto-Indo-European *-r̥
Proto-Indo-European *wódr̥
Proto-Balto-Slavic *wandō
Proto-Slavic *voda
Old Church Slavonic вода (voda)
Bulgarian вода

    Inherited from Old Church Slavonic вода (voda), from Proto-Slavic *voda, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wandō, from Proto-Indo-European *wódr̥.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): [voˈda]
    • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
    • Rhymes: -da
    • Syllabification(key): во‧да
    • IPA(key): [ˈvɔdɐ]
    • Rhymes: -ɔdɐ
    • Syllabification(key): во‧да (Western dialects)

    Noun

    [edit]

    вода́ or во́да • (vodá or vóda) f (relational adjective во́ден, diminutive води́ца or води́чка)

    1. aqua, water (an inorganic compound (of molecular formula H2O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid; it is present naturally as rain, and found in rivers, lakes and seas; its solid form is ice and its gaseous form is steam)
      пря́сна вода́ ― prjásna vodá ― fresh water
      би́стра вода́ ― bístra vodá ― clear water
      сла́дка вода́ ― sládka vodá ― freshwater
      бра́кична вода́ ― brákična vodá ― brackish water
      соле́на вода́ ― soléna vodá ― seawater
    2. (collective) body of water
      Synonyms: водое́м (vodoém), ва́па (vápa)
    3. (uncountable) water (as a medium, opposed to land)
      Antonym: су́ша (súša)
      Жи́ви същества́ населя́ват су́шата и вода́та.
      Žívi sǎštestvá naseljávat súšata i vodáta.
      Living creatures inhabit the land and the water.
    4. (usually in the plural) waters (territorial; specific body of water)
      териториа́лни води́
      teritoriálni vodí
      territorial waters
    5. solution, lotion, infusion, water (liquid extract)
      ро́зова вода́
      rózova vodá
      rose water
      йо́дна вода́
      jódna vodá
      iodine solution
    6. (colloquial, medicine) fluid, effusion (accumulated in the body due to illness)
      И́ма вода́ в коля́ното.
      Íma vodá v koljánoto.
      He has fluid on the knee.
    7. (figuratively, dated) padding, verbiage, fluff (superfluous text or speech)
      Synonyms: бала́ст (balást), многосло́вие (mnogoslóvie)

    Usage notes

    [edit]

    In dialects with free accent, the secondary form во́да (vóda) is used only in the role of grammatical object. Technically, it reflects the archaic mobile accentuation of acc. *vȍdǫ.

          [edit]

          Etymology

          [edit]

          From Old East Slavic вода (voda), from Proto-Slavic *voda, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wandō, from Proto-Indo-European *wódr̥.

          Noun

          [edit]

          вода́ • (vodá) f inan

          1. water

          Pannonian Rusyn

          [edit]

          Etymology

          [edit]

          Inherited from Old Slovak voda, from Proto-Slavic *voda. Cognates include Slovak voda and Carpathian Rusyn вода́ (vodá).

          Pronunciation

          [edit]
          • IPA(key): [ˈvɔda]
          • Rhymes: -ɔda
          • Hyphenation: во‧да

          Noun

          [edit]

          вода (voda) f (diminutive водичка or водица, relational adjective водов or водови)

          1. water
          2. flood, deluge

          locative води (vodi) водох (vodox)
          vocative вода (voda) води (vodi)

          Etymology 1

          [edit]
          Etymology tree
          Proto-Indo-European *wed-
          Proto-Indo-European *-r̥

          Old East Slavic вода (voda)
          Russian вода

            Inherited from Old East Slavic вода (voda), from Proto-Slavic *voda, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wandō, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *wódr̥. Cognates include Sanskrit उद्र (udra), Ancient Greek ὕδωρ (húdōr) → English hydro-, English whisky and water.

            Pronunciation

            [edit]
            • IPA(key): [vɐˈda]
            • Audio:(file)
            • Rhymes: -a

            Noun

            [edit]

            вода́ • (vodá) f inan (genitive воды́, nominative plural во́ды, genitive plural вод, relational adjective водяно́й or во́дный, diminutive води́чка or води́ца)

            1. water
              на воде́ и на су́ше ― na vodé i na súše ― by sea and by land
              лезть/поле́зть в во́ду ― leztʹ/poléztʹ v vódu ― to get into the water
              стака́н воды́ ― stakán vodý ― glass of water
              боло́тная вода́ ― bolótnaja vodá ― stagnant water
              спуск воды́ из туале́тного бачка́ ― spusk vodý iz tualétnovo bačká ― flushing the toilet
              под водо́й ― pod vodój ― underwater
            2. soft drink, soda
              со́ки и во́ды ― sóki i vódy ― juices and sodas
            3. (Northern Russia) tide
              ма́лая вода́ ― málaja vodá ― low tide
            4. (figuratively) watery prose, fluff
              Места́ми интере́сно, а всё остально́е — вода́.
              Mestámi interésno, a vsjo ostalʹnóje — vodá.
              Interesting in some places, but the rest is fluff.
